title: Finite presentations of finitely generated commutative monoids
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative monoid, written additively with identity $0$, and let $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ be a finite generating tuple, allowing $n=0$. Write $\pi:\mathbf N^n\to R$ for the surjective homomorphism $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i r_i$. Then there are finitely many pairs $(a_j,b_j)\in\mathbf N^n\times\mathbf N^n$, $1\leq j\leq m$, with $\pi(a_j)=\pi(b_j)$ such that the relation $\pi(a)=\pi(b)$ is the smallest monoid congruence containing these pairs. Here a monoid congruence is an equivalence relation preserved by addition, and smallest means the intersection of all such congruences containing the pairs. Equivalently, for any commutative monoid $T$ and tuple $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in T$, the assignment $r_i\mapsto t_i$ extends to a unique homomorphism $R\to T$ if and only if $\sum_i (a_j)_i t_i=\sum_i (b_j)_i t_i$ for all $j$. No integrality or saturation hypothesis on $R$ is needed.

proof.text: Let $M=\mathbf N^n$ and let $c=\ker(\pi)$, so $c(a,b)$ means $\pi(a)=\pi(b)$. Form the monoid algebra $A=\mathbf Z[M]$, identified with the polynomial ring $\mathbf Z[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] (whose monomials $x^\alpha$, $\alpha\in\mathbf N^n$, multiply by $x^\alpha x^\beta=x^{\alpha+\beta}$) by sending the basis element $[e_i]$ to $x_i$. The induced algebra map $\Phi:A\to\mathbf Z[R]$ sends $[a]$ to $[\pi(a)]$. By the monoid-algebra congruence-kernel lemma [lem-trf-congruence-polynomial-kernel], $\ker\Phi$ is the ideal generated by all binomials $[a]-[b]$ with $c(a,b)$.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; the monoid-algebra translation and kernel notation are written explicitly here.

proof.text: The ring $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-trf-mvpolynomial-noetherian]. Hence the ideal $I=\ker\Phi$ is generated by finitely many elements $f_1,\ldots,f_s$. Each $f_i$ lies in the ideal generated by the binomials $[a]-[b]$ from step 1, so its membership is witnessed by a finite sum involving only finitely many such binomials. Taking the union of those finite sets over $i=1,\ldots,s$ gives finitely many pairs $(a_j,b_j)$ with $c(a_j,b_j)$, and their binomials generate $I$.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; finite generation of an ideal and finite extraction from an ideal span are the elementary ideal argument.

proof.text: Let $d$ be the smallest congruence on $M$ containing the selected pairs. Every selected binomial vanishes after passage to the monoid quotient $M/d$, so the quotient map induces a homomorphism $A\to\mathbf Z[M/d]$ whose kernel contains $I$. Conversely, if $d(a,b)$ then the congruence-kernel lemma gives $[a]-[b]$ in the ideal generated by the selected differences, hence in $I$. Applying the same lemma to the quotient map shows that $[a]-[b]\in I$ forces $d(a,b)$: distinct $d$-classes are distinct basis vectors in $\mathbf Z[M/d]$, so their difference cannot vanish. Thus $c=d$, proving that the displayed finite pairs generate the relation $\pi(a)=\pi(b)$ as the smallest congruence.

source.place: Con.mk'_ker and quotient construction; the basis-vector separation argument for the monoid algebra is written explicitly here.

proof.text: For a commutative monoid $T$ and elements $t_i\in T$, the free commutative monoid map $\tau:M\to T$ sends $a$ to $\sum_i a_i t_i$. Since $\pi$ is surjective, a homomorphism $R\to T$ extending $r_i\mapsto t_i$ exists exactly when $\tau$ is constant on the fibres of $\pi$, equivalently when $c(a,b)$ implies $\tau(a)=\tau(b)$. Because $c$ is generated by the selected pairs, this is equivalent to the finitely many equations $\tau(a_j)=\tau(b_j)$. When it exists, uniqueness follows from surjectivity of $\pi$.

lean.statement: theorem fg_commutative_monoid_finite_presentation (R : Type u) [AddCommMonoid R] (n : ℕ) (r : Fin n → R) (π : (Fin n →₀ ℕ) →+ R) (hπ : Function.Surjective π) (hπ_formula : ∀ a : Fin n →₀ ℕ, π a = a.sum (fun i k => k • r i)) : ∃ (m : ℕ) (ab : Fin m → (Fin n →₀ ℕ) × (Fin n →₀ ℕ)), (∀ j : Fin m, π (ab j).1 = π (ab j).2) ∧ (∀ a b : Fin n →₀ ℕ, π a = π b ↔ ∀ c : AddCon (Fin n →₀ ℕ), (∀ j : Fin m, c (ab j).1 (ab j).2) → c a b) ∧ (∀ (T : Type v) [AddCommMonoid T] (t : Fin n → T), (∃! f : R →+ T, ∀ i : Fin n, f (r i) = t i) ↔ ∀ j : Fin m, (ab j).1.sum (fun i k => k • t i) = (ab j).2.sum (fun i k => k • t i))
